## Data

For this assignment, I will use a dataset of bigfood sightings from Kaggle:

Link to the data set: [Bigfoot Sightings](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/thedevastator/unlocking-mysteries-of-bigfoot-through-sightings)

```{r Intro, echo: false}
library(tidyverse)
library(DT)
```

## Reading the Data from Github

```{r Chunk1}

# Load the bfro_locations.csv file

bigfoot <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MarcinKayfromBK/DATA-607-MarcinK/refs/heads/main/bfro_locations.csv")

#The raw data loads with two null columns at the end so let's delete them. 
bigfoot <- bigfoot[, -c(8,9)]

datatable(bigfoot)


```

## Capability 1: Converting Characters to Numbers in Column 6 with Mutate

**Dplyr** is a Tidyverse package in R for data manipulation designed to make working with data frames and tibbles fast, readable, and intuitive. Part of the [tidyverse](https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/) suite, it provides a consistent set of function "verbs" that translate your data analysis thoughts directly into code.

**Mutate()** is a function in the dplyr package is used to create, modify, or delete columns in a data frame. It applies a transformation to your data while keeping the total number of rows intact and preserving all other existing columns

# Example

```{r Chunk2}

# In this chunk, we will use the mutate function to convert latitude into a numeric column. From the original CSV data, longitude is automatically imported as numeric but latitude comes in as a character. 

bigfoot <- bigfoot %>%
  mutate(across(latitude, as.numeric))

```

## Capability 2: Slice Function from Dplyr

The **Slice()** function is used to select, remove, or duplicate rows of a dataframe by their integer positions rather than by logical conditions.

# Example

```{r Chunk3}

bigfoot %>% slice(c(15:18, 35, 140:145)) # Passed as a vector

```

## Capability 3: Cleaning Column 5 with Lubridate

**Lubridate** is a Tidyverse package that makes it easier to work with dates and times in R. As of the latest tidyverse release, lubridate is part of core tidyverse.

**ymd_hms()** is a core function in the R package lubridate designed to parse character or numeric vectors into POSIXct date-time objects.

# Example

```{r Chunk4}

# Load the bfro_locations.csv file

bigfoot <- bigfoot %>% 
  mutate(timestamp_dttm = ymd_hms(timestamp))

```
